newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate down further, baht firms late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate down further, baht firms late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate continued to ease to 10.75-11.00 percent in late trade on Tuesday from 11.25-11.50 earlier and 12.00 late on Monday on rising liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers said heavy dollar selling today and some inflow of foreign funds also helped raise market liquidity.
"If the dollar selling remained heavy and foreign inflowa continue to persist, the interbank rate may fall below 10.00 percent this week," one dealer at a local bank said.
The baht edged up to 25.408-25.413 to the dollar late active trade compared with 25.413-25.416 in early morning on dollar's weakness abroad, dealers said.
"There was heavy selling of the dollar today after the U.S. unit's fall against other major currencies. The continuing inflow of foreign funds was also felt," said one currency dealer.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium fell to 8.25/9.00 satangs late from 9.00/10.00 in the morning on improving liquidity, dealers said.
The baht/dollar mid-rate was fixed by the Bank of Thailand at 25.43 against 25.42 on Monday. The mid-rate of 25.43 was the lowest level set since February 10, 1994.
